title: Ledger and Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Ashford's founding patriarch, Elias Verne, is exhumed for a sesquicentennial ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Jude Fairweather discovers that Verne's death certificate was signed by the same doctor linked to three 'accidental' deaths Jude has already quietly solved. Digging into the town's founding ledger, Jude uncovers a pattern: every generation, someone who threatened to expose the Verne family's original crime — a land swindle built on a murdered partner — dies conveniently. The killer is not one person but an inherited duty, passed down and currently held by the town's beloved archivist, Ruth Verne-Calloway, who has been protecting the family name her whole life. In the end, Jude corners Ruth in the sealed crypt where Elias's body was secretly moved decades ago; she confesses on his recorder, then chooses to walk into the rising river rather than face trial, leaving Jude to publish the truth at the cost of the town's identity — and his own peace.
about_author: B. M. Quintana is a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering courtrooms and county archives before turning to fiction. They live near the coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy fascination with municipal record rooms.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Jude's POV. At the sesquicentennial exhumation, the coffin lid opens on nothing but century-old air. Jude, attending for podcast material, notices the crowd's fear rather than shock. Emotional beat: unease — the town mourns a man whose body was never there.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In his home studio, Jude reviews the three deaths he solved off-record: a drowned surveyor, a burned tenant farmer, a fallen clerk. Each file carries Dr. Aldous Prewitt's signature. Beat: quiet vindication curdling into dread as he connects the fourth signature.

chapters.title: The Sesquicentennial Committee
chapters.summary: Jude interviews committee chair Mayor Doris Hale, who wants the empty-coffin story buried before it buries tourism. She stonewalls but lets slip that the exhumation order came from inside the historical society. Beat: frustration sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ruth of the Archives
chapters.summary: Introduce Ruth Verne-Calloway, town archivist and Verne descendant, warm and formidable. She helps Jude pull Elias Verne's death records — too helpfully, steering him away from 1874. Beat: charm with a blade under it.

chapters.title: The Founding Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude finds the founding ledger lists four names on the original land grant, though history remembers only Verne. The fourth name, Amos Kettle, was erased. Beat: the thrill of the hunt rekindled.

chapters.title: A Body That Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ground-penetrating radar (a favor from a listener) shows an unmarked vault beneath the old Verne chapel. Someone moved the body long ago — deliberately, carefully. Beat: cold awe at how deep the cover-up goes.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Descendants
chapters.summary: Jude tracks Prewitt's descendants; the last one, an elderly nurse, recalls her grandmother burning papers 'for the family.' She gives him one surviving page: a payment record from Verne estate to Prewitt, dated after the death certificate. Beat: the case turns from mystery to conspiracy.

chapters.title: What Amos Kettle Left
chapters.summary: Jude visits the last Kettle, a recluse named Tom, who hands over letters proving Amos was Verne's partner — and threatened to go to the press in 1875. He died within the month. Beat: grief across generations; Tom just wants his name back.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred
chapters.summary: Jude airs a careful episode about the empty coffin without naming suspects. Downloads explode; so do threats. His landlord asks him to leave. Beat: the cost of speaking begins to mount.

chapters.title: The First Threat
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A note in period handwriting appears on his windshield: 'Some ledgers balance themselves.' The ink is modern; the hand is practiced, antique. Beat: fear made personal.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mayor Hale offers Jude access to sealed council minutes if he delays the next episode until after Founders' Day. He refuses; she warns him the town eats its historians. Beat: moral crossroads.

chapters.title: The Chapel Vault
chapters.summary: Night break-in chapter. Jude opens the chapel vault and finds not Elias Verne but a second coffin — Amos Kettle's, hidden beneath the founder's nameplate. Beat: vertigo; the town's whole story is inverted.

chapters.title: Interrupted
chapters.summary: Someone arrives mid-break-in. Jude hides, glimpses a figure in a long coat laying fresh flowers on the wrong coffin. He escapes unseen but drops his recorder. Beat: heart-pounding near-capture.

chapters.title: The Missing Recorder
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The recorder is gone from where he dropped it. Whoever took it now knows his voice, his notes, his theory. Beat: paranoia tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Drowned Again
chapters.summary: Tom Kettle is found dead in the river — the same method as the 1960s surveyor. Ruled accidental. Jude recognizes the signature move. Beat: rage and guilt; his questions got a man killed.

chapters.title: Sheriff Okafor
chapters.summary: Introduce Sheriff Adaeze Okafor, honest but politically cornered. She privately admits the drowning doesn't sit right and shares an old unsolved file. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: relief of finally having one ally.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Okafor and Jude find Verne's will contains a secret codicil funding 'maintenance of family honor' in perpetuity — a trust paying an annual stipend to an unnamed custodian. Beat: the horror of institutionalized murder.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Jude traces the trust through shell foundations to a current account. The withdrawals are small, regular, and recent. The custodian is alive and active. Beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Public set-piece. Jude attends the festival watching everyone, cataloguing who avoids him. Ruth gives a stirring speech about legacy. Beat: dramatic irony thick enough to taste.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: An anonymous envelope contains a 1970s photo: young Ruth standing over the reopened grave with her father. Jude realizes the duty passed mother to daughter, generation to generation. Beat: pity invading his suspicion.

chapters.title: Ruth's Version
chapters.summary: Ruth invites Jude for tea and tells a half-truth: yes, her family hid things, but only shame, she claims — never bodies. Her composure cracks exactly once, at Amos's name. Beat: the interviewer interviewed.

chapters.title: The Second Coffin's Secret
chapters.summary: Forensics (via Okafor) date the chapel burial to the 1920s — meaning the body-swap happened generations after Elias died, and more than once. There were multiple custodians. Beat: scale of the lie expands.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Jude's apartment catches fire while he's out retrieving evidence from a safe-deposit box. He loses everything but the ledger photocopies in his bag. Beat: survival stripped to essentials; the price theme lands hard.

chapters.title: Off the Grid
chapters.summary: Jude holes up in Tom Kettle's cabin, broadcasting nothing, working from paper. He maps every custodian-era death against trust disbursements — they align perfectly. Beat: grim clarity; the pattern is complete.

chapters.title: Okafor Under Pressure
chapters.summary: The sheriff is suspended pending an 'integrity review' after Jude's episodes. She meets him anyway, off-duty, and gives him the trust's beneficiary file she copied before losing access. Beat: sacrifice; justice outside the law needs insiders.

chapters.title: The Beneficiary File
chapters.summary: The file names the current stipend recipient via a code — 'Custodian V.' Cross-referencing signatures on historical society documents, Jude matches the hand on his windshield threat. It's Ruth's. Beat: confirmation without triumph.

chapters.title: Why She Does It
chapters.summary: Jude researches Ruth's life: orphaned young, raised by the previous custodian, her entire identity built on guardianship of the Verne legend. Beat: tragic comprehension — she isn't evil; she's inherited.

chapters.title: The Trap He Sets
chapters.summary: Jude leaks a fake detail: that he's found Elias's actual remains and will announce where, publicly, on Sunday. Only the custodian would need to act. Beat: hunter becomes bait knowingly.

chapters.title: Sunday at the Chapel
chapters.summary: Stakeout chapter. Ruth comes at dawn, alone, carrying a shovel. Instead of destroying remains, she kneels and prays at both coffins. Jude steps out. Beat: confrontation deferred by grief.

chapters.title: Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: In the chapel, Ruth talks — about her father teaching her that some truths rot a town from the roots, about the first time she helped move a coffin at nineteen. Recorded again, this time willingly. Beat: devastating intimacy.

chapters.title: Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Ruth admits Tom Kettle's death wasn't hers — there is another custodian-in-waiting, her grandnephew Daniel, whom she trained and can no longer control. Beat: the twist; the system outlived even its keeper.

chapters.title: Daniel
chapters.summary: Jude and Okafor race to find Daniel Calloway, a charming historical society volunteer who has been feeding Jude helpful clues all along — grooming him toward a fall. Beat: betrayal reframing earlier chapters.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Daniel plants evidence implicating Jude in Tom Kettle's death; Okafor's suspension is weaponized; a warrant issues for Jude. Beat: net closing from every direction.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger
chapters.summary: Fugitive chapter. Using the trust paper trail, Jude proves Daniel accessed the stipend account twice recently — Daniel has been taking money and staging deaths to force Ruth's hand. Beat: clarity under pressure.

chapters.title: The Crypt
chapters.summary: Jude deduces Daniel will destroy both coffins and the codicil during Founders' Day fireworks, when the chapel will be empty and loud. He goes in alone rather than wait for a police force that wants him cuffed. Beat: deliberate descent.

chapters.title: Ledger and Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax. In the crypt, Daniel attacks; Ruth intervenes, taking a blow meant for Jude, and holds Daniel while Jude records Daniel's boasting confession. Fire spreads from Daniel's accelerant. Beat: violence, loyalty, and truth fused.

chapters.title: The River
chapters.summary: Rescue and aftermath of the fire. Ruth, injured and exposed, slips away during the chaos. Jude finds her at the riverbank. She thanks him for giving the dead their names back — then walks into the water before he can reach her. Beat: tragedy; the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: What the Town Deserves
chapters.summary: Okafor, reinstated after Daniel's arrest, must decide what to release. She and Jude agree: everything, including Ruth's recorded confession. Beat: justice chosen over comfort, jointly.

chapters.title: Amos Kettle, Restored
chapters.summary: The town reels; the historical society re-carves the founders' monument with four names. Tom Kettle receives a headstone. Jude publishes the final episode, raw and unresolved. Beat: mourning turned into repair.

chapters.title: The Next Cold Case
chapters.summary: Epilogue, months later. Jude, living above the new archive Ruth willed to the public, receives an envelope: another impossible death, another town. He weighs the cost — and starts recording. Beat: bittersweet forward motion; the work continues.
